claims.title: Exact progressive classical query-revelation tradeoff
claims.scope: binary records partitioned into nonempty query-hint cells, one finite shared message before the hint, one finite selected branch message after the cell hint, and an exact coordinate query afterward
assumptions: the partition cells are disjoint and cover every record coordinate
the shared message has at most 2^a values and branch j has at most 2^c_j values
every record and every later coordinate in the revealed cell must be answered with zero error
nonclaims: the theorem does not cover overlapping hint sets or noisy hints
message bits in the internal interface are not parent-universe hardware bits

claims.title: Branch-aware bounded-error progressive information converse
claims.scope: independent uniform binary record coordinates with declared coordinate errors under one shared and one hint-selected branch message
assumptions: coordinate decoders use the shared message and the selected cell message
binary Fano, data processing, and conditional entropy subadditivity apply
the source blocks induced by partition cells are independent
nonclaims: the information inequality is necessary and is not asserted to be finite-block achievable for every error profile
correlated or nonuniform source records require a different entropy calculation

claims.title: Unassisted quantum progressive-query tradeoff
claims.scope: the same progressive coordinate-query interface with unassisted transmitted quantum systems in the shared and branch stages
assumptions: the receiver has no preshared system correlated with the encoder
a q-qubit message has classical mutual-information contribution at most q bits
later coordinate answers are obtained by measurements after the selected branch system arrives
nonclaims: the continuum of quantum state vectors is not treated as unbounded retrievable classical capacity
internal qubits are not identified with parent-substrate qubits

claims.title: Entanglement-assisted progressive-query factor-two tradeoff
claims.scope: progressive quantum messages with receiver-side preshared entanglement independent of the later binary record
assumptions: each transmitted qubit can increase receiver classical mutual information by at most two bits
dense coding is available for the exact achievability construction
the storage and distribution of preshared entanglement are outside the transmitted-qubit count
nonclaims: preshared entanglement is not claimed to be physically free
the factor-two capacity does not remove linear dependence on residual query-cell size

claims.title: Residual query-cell communication law
claims.scope: equal-size query-hint cells with communication permitted after the cell hint but before the exact coordinate query
assumptions: one selected branch is executed per run
the per-run objective counts the common message plus the selected branch message
all cells have the same size s
nonclaims: the result depends on the query-hint timing and does not apply when no later branch communication is possible
the residual requirement scales with cell size rather than the logarithm of cell size

claims.title: Progressive query-timing phase diagram
claims.scope: the declared partition-hint model ranging from one unresolved cell to singleton cells
assumptions: the hint reveals exactly one partition cell
the exact coordinate is revealed only after the branch message
nonclaims: query-hint entropy and record-value information are distinct resources
the phase diagram is not a model of actual cosmological observation scheduling

claims.title: Finite exact progressive-protocol certificate
claims.scope: explicit bounded binary records under the canonical uncovered-bit allocation constructed by the repository
assumptions: complete enumeration is capped at the declared maximum record length
shared and branch coordinate allocations are disjoint and cover every cell
nonclaims: finite enumeration does not establish unrelated multiround protocols
the checker validates the declared construction rather than an empirical physical system
